pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks all rows are 0 and the CHECK constraint.
test 'AC-2' covers / and ?view=open with id order.
test 'AC-3' covers done-only, ✓ prefix, id order (marks 3,1).
test 'AC-4' covers all items, marks and order.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav for each view and /.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__.
test 'AC-7' covers the empty table in every view and both empty-view messages.
traffic/routes.json lists both views; test 'AC-8' checks it. The traffic test that proves the worker actually requests them was weakened (see findings), but the AC-8 text only requires listing.

findings.what: The last commit ('Follow-up edits') replaced `expect(app.seen.map(s => s.path)).toEqual(["/healthz", ...ROUTES])` with `.toBeDefined()`, which can never fail. The test no longer checks that the traffic worker requests /healthz and every listed route, including the new query routes. No spec decision justifies loosening it.
findings.fix: Restore the toEqual assertion. The fakeApp already records pathname+search, so it works with the query routes.

findings.what: The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the final commit loosened the synthetic-traffic assertion to toBeDefined(). The claim is false.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion, or state the loosening and its reason.

findings.what: The empty-table check runs an extra COUNT query on every empty open or done view. This is acceptable, but it makes a second DB round trip.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec's intent and decisions: the list opens on open items, and the view is a query parameter.
All 8 ACs have named tests, and every state row has a test. The traffic assertion was weakened afterwards.
The traffic test was reduced to toBeDefined(), which can never fail.
The README describes the views. The new migration and routes are covered.
The view value is validated with Object.hasOwn, and titles are escaped. No defects found.
The view value is allowlisted and never interpolated into SQL, since only VIEWS fragments are used. Output is escaped.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML, with no UI framework or styling files in the diff.
The PR has no browser or screenshots, and the diff touches no UI components beyond the HTML template.
The claim 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' is false.
